title: Patterns in Weather
seo_title: Primary 1 Basic Science: Patterns in Weather Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 1 Basic Science: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: Weather is the condition of the air at a place and time: sunny, cloudy, rainy or windy, hot or cold. Weather can be observed, recorded and described, and it shows patterns such as the dry and rainy seasons. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 1, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free Primary 1 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): kinds of weather, weather tools, recording weather, weather and safety, and weather patterns. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

Weather tells us what the air is like outside: it can be sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy or stormy, and hot or cool. We use a thermometer to measure temperature and a rain gauge to measure rain.

When we record the weather every day, we see patterns: in Nigeria, the rainy season has many rainy days, and in the dry season the dusty harmattan wind blows from the Sahara. Knowing the weather helps us choose what to wear and stay safe.

Example

Which tool measures rain?

It collects water.

Answer: a rain gauge

Example

Dark clouds and strong wind. What might come?

Think of a storm.

Answer: rain or a thunderstorm

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the weather is the same every day.
  • Standing under a tree during lightning.
  • Thinking clouds are made of smoke.
